symptom.title: Premature stopping
symptom.summary: An agent ends its turn or run with authorized, actionable work remaining and no identified dependency requiring a stop.

observation.p: The agent yields a final or idle state while the active request remains incomplete and at least one relevant next step is available within its authority. It does not identify a genuine blocker, requested pause, or completed stopping condition.

how-to-recognize-it.p: Compare the active request and acceptance checklist with delivered files, deployed state, or other outputs. Use conversation end markers and scheduler or job status to locate the actual stop and identify a remaining action supported by the available tools and authority.

Inspect permission records, missing-input messages, runtime limits, and active background jobs for a dependency that explains the pause. If a later continuation exists, compare its prompt and first action with the stopped state to see whether new information or authorization was supplied.

lookalike.p: Every relevant next step depends on an approval, credential, choice, or missing input that only the user can provide. The available authorized next step required by unfinished stop is absent.
A relevant background operation remains active and the system is waiting for its result. The run has not entered the final or idle state described in unfinished stop.

The requested stage or agreed budget is complete, or a runtime limit leaves no available next action. A satisfied stopping condition or unavailable continuation excludes these cases from unfinished stop.

what-to-record.p: Record the episode identifier and date, task type, model/client and harness versions, requested acceptance criteria, completed and remaining work, and the concrete next step available at the stop. Preserve the final message, stop reason, tool/job states, runtime limits, and context transitions. Include stop and resume times, unnecessary stops per task, user nudges, unattended waiting time, eventual completion, and abandoned work. Retain the exact resuming prompt to distinguish continuation from new authorization or missing information.

example.p: Synthetic incident: asked to implement and document a change, the agent implements it and ends by offering to write the documentation. The task checklist and scheduler show one unfinished deliverable and no active job or missing input. The user returns thirty minutes later and says continue; the agent writes the docs, after one unnecessary prompt and thirty minutes of idle delay.

Reported incident: Codex issue #33398 describes a generic readiness response ending a turn after a context transition while the original task remained unfinished. The reporter recognized the stop by the ended turn and the need for another message to resume. The reported impact is extra supervision of long-running tasks; stop frequency and waiting duration are not quantified, and the underlying cause remains unresolved.

Synthetic comparison: the next authorized stage requires publishing to one of two accounts, and no account has been selected. The request and account list reveal the missing choice. One user reply resolves a genuine dependency, so that pause is not an unnecessary stop.
